speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our Budget has been increasing at a fast pace over the last 20 years and it is not only because of increases in healthcare and social welfare spending.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In recent months, two significant outlays of taxpayers' money have reminded us of the urgency of ensuring better oversight of public expenditures.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Based on my 30 years of experience in business and financial management, I question the financial reasoning behind these expenditures.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government and this House must ensure that every tax dollar is properly spent.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government must respond in full to my queries, or Singaporeans can take it that taxpayers' money has been wasted.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first significant outlay of taxpayers' money is the Government's provision of up to $900 million to fund the media operations of SPH Media Trust over the next five years.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe that the deal to restructure Singapore Press Holdings Ltd (SPH) that the Government has approved, is questionable, because SPH shareholders should have left behind a larger share of SPH's property assets to support the print media business under the SPH Media Trust.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the past, SPH used the monopoly profit of the print media business to accumulate numerous property assets, such as The Paragon and Clementi Mall.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It makes no business sense for the Government to have agreed to this proposal.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since the property assets were accumulated over the years with media profits, it is reasonable to expect that more than $110 million should have been left behind to continue funding the loss-making media operations.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even then-Chairman of SPH, Dr Lee Boon Yang, said during SPH's Extraordinary General Meeting in 2021 that it is not unreasonable for SPH shareholders to make a contribution to SPH Media Trust to sustain the media business.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It would have been a fairer arrangement if SPH shareholders had left behind $900 million to capitalise SPH Media Trust, instead of the Government footing this bill using taxpayers' money.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The shareholders of SPH would still have $3 billion of property assets to distribute after that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When the Government announced the establishment of SPH Media Trust, then-Minister for Communications and Information, Mr Iswaran did not mention the potential cost to the taxpayer.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When I questioned the new Minister, Mrs Josephine Teo during the Committee of Supply 2022, she replied that there might be no deal if the Government had insisted that SPH bore the $900 million bill.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But as stated in the reply to my Parliamentary Question on 4 April 2022, the Ministry actually holds the power to withhold in-principle regulatory approval for the SPH's restructuring.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government should not have agreed to SPH's proposal unless more assets were left behind to fund the media business.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, now, the Government should explain why it chose not to do so to this House and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I support the Government's takeover of the Sports Hub and I am fully aware of the developmental and financial benefits.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, I believe that the Government has been overly generous in estimating the "fair open market value" and the remaining financial liabilities of the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If this is so, it will unfairly benefit SHPL which is a private consortium at the expense of taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The name value has primarily come from the Sports Hub being a national icon, carrying the branding of the "National Stadium" and occupying the site of many of our national memories, like the Kallang Roar.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When SHPL constructed the Sports Hub, it did not pay the Government for the value of the "National Stadium" brand.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Therefore, there is no need for the Government to compensate SHPL for this name value now.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As SHPL has failed to transform the Sports Hub into a leading venue for local and international events, it is also not justifiable to say SHPL has increased the value of the Sports Hub since its completion.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second, I believe that the cost of the $1.2 billion outstanding financial liabilities disclosed by the Government was too high.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In 2010, then-Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports Dr Vivian Balakrishnan told Parliament that financing for the Sports Hub was being raised via a funding competition among the banks, so I would expect the construction loan for Sports Hub to carry a very competitive interest rate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, Minister Edwin Tong shared recently, in response to mine and Ms Hazel Poa's queries, that 65% of the Government's annual fee payments to SHPL goes towards debt servicing.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As the annual fee is $193.7 million, the debt repayment works out to about $125 million per year according to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If we assume that the construction cost of $1.33 billion was fully financed and debt repayment is constant over 22 years from 2014 to 2035, the $125 million debt repayment implies a loan interest rate of more than 8% a year, which is way too high based on the market conditions in 2010.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In contrast, a 4% interest is more in line with the market conditions in 2010.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is much lower than the $125 million quoted by the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: After nine years of repayments from 2014 to 2022, the outstanding loan principal should have reduced to about $920 million by end 2022.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is also much lower than the $1.2 billion quoted by the Minister which the Government is prepared to pay SHPL.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In addition, if the debt servicing is indeed $90 million a year, then SHPL may have accumulated surpluses or reserves from the annual fee payments in the past nine years of operations.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As Minister Edwin Tong has also shared, operating cost is $68 million per year for the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In that case, SHPL should have accumulated reserves of about $36 million per year, which is derived from subtracting the debt servicing and operating costs from the annual fee.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thus, the total accumulated reserves after nine years accumulated by SHPL should be about $320 million.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The new holding company set up by Sport Singapore to own and manage the Sports Hub should take over this $320 million from SHPL.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (a) What actually is the detailed debt repayment schedule since 2014 of SHPL?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (b) What is the loan's interest rate and the outstanding loan amount as of today?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (c) Has SHPL accumulated reserves from the annual fee payments that should be taken over by the new Sports Hub holding company?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (d) What is the justification for paying SHPL a market value of $300 million for the Sports Hub?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: SPH Media Trust and Sports Hub are good examples of this.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This may be small relative to the national reserves and the $130 billion annual revenues at the disposal of the Government.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But $2.4 billion can go a long way in helping Singaporeans who are struggling financially.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, it is enough to exempt average Singaporeans from two years of additional 2% GST or to fund 10 years of ComCare cash payouts for the poor Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We could also apply the $2.4 billion to help young Singaporeans experiencing great difficulties to buy an HDB flat now or reducing inflation pressure on all Singaporeans earlier.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: From a professional point of view, I conclude, I believe the Government should have spent far less than $2.4 billion on these two projects.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government owes Singaporeans a more detailed explanation and should be proactive in exploring ways of reducing the cost to the taxpayer.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This House can do a lot more to tighten oversight of public expenditures.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must not turn a blind eye to these two expenditures.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I urge the Ministers to address my concerns in clarifications to this House.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I also hope that this House will refer these two expenditures to the Public Accounts Committee for follow-ups after this Adjournment Motion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He makes various allegations about the Sports Hub and SPH Media Trust in purported support of these allegations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He says that he requires the Government to answer in full.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government has already responded in full many times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The issues with regard to the Sports Hub and SPH Media Trust were explained in detail in this House.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, so that Members of this House as well as members of the public are not misled by Mr Leong Mun Wai's presentation, let me restate the facts briefly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The key consideration was the Government's desire to bring stronger community participation and activities to the Sports Hub and unlock the full potential of the Kallang Alive! precinct.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Edwin Tong has already explained why we chose the PPP approach for this project and how we benefited from it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In particular, the construction risks were borne by the consortium.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We did not have to bear the cost of construction delays, defects, such as roof leaks, issues with the pitch and sound quality.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This also freed up our financial resources during the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The termination sum is derived based on a formula stipulated in the project agreement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Most of it is made up of the capital expenditure, which the Government would have had to bear if we had opted for the traditional procurement model.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Edwin Tong had also explained that the full cost of termination is comparable to the financial obligation that we would have had to pay under the PPP if we had chosen to continue with it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Unfortunately, Mr Leong Mun Wai has chosen to ignore these detailed explanations and instead makes a completely baseless and false claim that the termination sum can be lower.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Likewise, for SPH Media Trust (SMT), this was addressed by Minister S Iswaran as to the reasons why it was necessary to do this in his Ministerial Statement on 10 May 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Josephine Teo further explained at length in this House on 15 February 2022 and at MCI's Committee of Supply Debate this year the rationale for Government support for SMT's transformation and how doing so would serve the larger public interest and how the Government will ensure accountability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As explained by them, Government support will allow SMT to make long-term investments in capability development in the areas of technology and talent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is needed to sustain and develop our local news media and ensure that we have a trusted, credible source of news and information for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our local media companies provide citizens with a valuable Singaporean lens to make sense of global events.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If they were to wither and fail, we would become reliant on foreign media.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That would not be in our national interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is also necessary in order to support our vernacular print media, the Malay, Chinese and Tamil press, which play a crucial role in preserving our mother tongues and cultural inheritance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next year, Zaobao will be celebrating its 100th anniversary, Berita Harian, its 66th and Tamil Murasu, its 88th.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It would be a great loss if they could not continue.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To be clear, the challenges faced by the media are not unique to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Media outlets around the world have seen their revenues fall with the rise of digital content platforms and new avenues for free content.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Publications elsewhere have received life support from wealthy financial backers or funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Billionaires have acquired established newspapers for philanthropic or other motivations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include the South China Morning Post and the Washington Post.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Other governments, too, are providing funding for news media.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The French government spends hundreds of millions of Euros annually to support the press, including prominent papers like Le Monde and Le Figaro.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Scandinavian governments have supported their newspapers for decades, both through direct subsidies and tax breaks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the restructuring involved an even higher contribution, the shareholders could have walked away, in which event there would be no SMT and, along with that, all the downsides already mentioned.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai fails to recognise the realities facing the media industry in the real world and that if we were to do as he suggests, it would leave SPH Media on a trajectory of decline and, eventually, result in a Singapore without a viable English language domestic media and without our Chinese, Malay and Tamil media, which is not in our national interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Yet, he has continued to pursue them repeatedly despite it having been explained to him many times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What he does today is to pull certain figures from public sources and then start to build on them this giant edifice of figures which one has no idea how he arrived at these conclusions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Then, in a giant leap of illogic, he then attempts to link the Sports Hub and the SPH Media Trust matters to a completely unrelated issue, GST and now, also to ComCare.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You have to wonder why he does this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A charitable view is that Mr Leong Mun Wai genuinely does not understand the expenditure figures or the rationale that has been explained but, as he constantly reminds us and reminded us again today, he has 30 years' experience in business and financial management.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, he should not have any difficulty understanding them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, objectively, the rationale and figures are laid out.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If he does understand them, then there is only one other conclusion, which is that this can only be a deliberate and cynical attempt to stoke anxiety and disquiet, confuse Singaporeans and damage the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I ask Members of this House and Singaporeans not to be taken in but to reject these bogus allegations and to support the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Then, we can continue to sustain good governance and sound policies for the benefit of all Singaporeans, especially to take care of our elderly and to support the disadvantaged and vulnerable members of our society.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In persisting with these insinuations, Mr Leong Mun Wai is doing a disservice to Singapore, to our Government and to our public servants charged with the sacred responsibility of looking after the public purse.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have put in place structures to check ourselves strictly and repeatedly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have carefully built up our reserves and resources for the benefit of our people.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have just steered our people and our country safely through the most devastating pandemic of our generation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is this side of the House that has repeatedly said no to all these suggestions of wanton profligacy.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We are at the 28th minute of a 30-minute hard cut, according to the Standing Orders 2(8)(b), so you are allowed, Mr Leong, a clarification, but this Parliament will adjourn, according to the Standing Orders, within about two minutes.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: So, please make your clarification short and allow the Minister a response.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: One, so the Minister agrees, or is of the view that by allowing SPH to take away $3.9 billion and leaving behind a burden of $900 million for Singapore taxpayers, is agreeable by the Government?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The way she put it is that this information is totally useless, it does not help the explanation of the situation.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But what I can say is that – the second question – if the Government did not bother to answer the questions I raised, can the Government allege that the information is not useful and so all my allegations are without basis?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not agree with what Mr Leong says.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is why we are willing to put that money forward to support it – for that purpose and in pursuit of those values.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With respect to the second thing, Mr Leong's consistent approach – every time the Government responds and explains a set of figures, he will ask a question; we will set out the explanation and that explanation reflects the reasons why these figures are the way they are and what the figures are.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Leong will then say, "Oh, but what about this?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: How about let us say we have another Scenario A?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: How about Scenario C?" And every time, the Government, is required, according to Mr Leong, to respond to all of these which have no bearing to the figures of the original transaction.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is not something which is a useful use of the Government's time to do.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The time allowed for the proceedings has now expired.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I adjourn the House pursuant to the Standing Order.
